Now: one Stop hook (`stop-gates.sh`) deriving the change set once (`gate-context.sh`) and entering a gate only when the change set holds a path it could possibly gate; per-gate pass caches keyed on **that gate's own inputs**, so editing a spec file no longer re-runs the plugin-registry gates; one batched repo scan for every wiring candidate; one `awk` pass for genericity whatever the diff's size. Also fixed: two registry-gate false blocks (Windows Python's CRLF broke every `plugin.json` membership match; the gate flagged a variable named inside its own trailing comment). New env toggles `AFK_GATE_CTX_DISABLE`, `AFK_SKIP_PRECOMMIT_GATES`, `AFK_MAVEN_LOCK_WAIT`. **Restart the session** (hooks.json changed), and run a session in each existing checkout so `install-git-hooks.sh` adds the `pre-commit` hook. "- **Gates no longer tax interactive work.** A turn that only talked now costs one short-circuit check instead of the whole suite, and the three expensive code gates (`maven-compile`, `java-format`, `ui-lint`) moved off Stop onto a **`pre-commit`** git hook — same enforcement, paid once per commit instead of once per question. What made this necessary: gate latency on Windows/git-bash is **subprocess count**, not algorithm (MSYS fork emulation runs ~0.5–2s per spawn against ~20–40ms native, and degrades under load), and the suite was spawning hundreds — a cache key that re-hashed the tree with two forks per changed file, recomputed independently by all seven gates; a registry gate re-grepping the same files once per skill and once per env var; a wiring gate running a full-monorepo scan **per new file**. Now: one Stop hook (`stop-gates.sh`) deriving the change set once (`gate-context.sh`) and entering a gate only when the change set holds a path it could possibly gate; per-gate pass caches keyed on **that gate's own inputs**, so editing a spec file no longer re-runs the plugin-registry gates; one batched repo scan for every wiring candidate; one `awk` pass for genericity whatever the diff's size. Measured on the same tree: full cold Stop 56–95s (was over 2min, with the genericity gate alone recorded at 12min), unchanged tree 7.5–12.5s, and design-chain artifacts (PRD/SDD/plan/ADR/journal files) no longer report as wiring orphans — they have no textual referrer by construction. Also fixed: two registry-gate false blocks (Windows Python's CRLF broke every `plugin.json` membership match; the gate flagged a variable named inside its own trailing comment). New env toggles `AFK_GATE_CTX_DISABLE`, `AFK_SKIP_PRECOMMIT_GATES`, `AFK_MAVEN_LOCK_WAIT`. **Restart the session** (hooks.json changed), and run a session in each existing checkout so `install-git-hooks.sh` adds the `pre-commit` hook. Cost model + the rules a new gate must follow: `hooks/README.md`." | asserts a session run makes install-git-hooks.sh add the pre-commit hook; confirmed install-git-hooks.sh:102 and SessionStart wiring hooks/hooks.json:9

claims.text: Inference: the design round's claim that install_block.py 'has no Python importer' (docs/afk/setup-per-repo/design.round.json:510) holds for production code only. test_install_block.py loads the file by path and uses the private _target_lock, so moving the locked writer into a shared module breaks those tests unless they move with it. Likewise a rename of install-git-hooks.sh would stop the SessionStart install with no signal, because run-hook.py:1030-1032 treats a missing handler as optional.

install_block.py is invoked by two setup instructions: MANIFEST.md H7 Fix (`"$py" install_block.py install "$rendered" "$target" || exit 1`, once per enabled provider target, run when the human accepts the H7 opt-in in SKILL.md step 3/4), relying on a non-zero exit on failure (exit 2 + stderr `install_block: <exc>` for OSError/InstallError) and on the default sentinel `behaviors` plus the legacy set plain-language, lavish-sessions, investigation; and the SKILL.md teardown branch (`afk-python install_block.py teardown "$f"` for the two user instruction files), which checks no exit code and is judged done by AUDIT.md check 7.

Documents that send a reader to install_block.py teardown through `/afk:setup teardown`: PROVIDERS.md:121, README.md:274, CHANGELOG.md:556, AUDIT.md:136, MANIFEST.md:279-280; documents asserting the afk:behaviors block the installer writes: AGENTS.md:83, GLOSSARY.md:87, PROVIDERS.md:34, CHANGELOG.md:554, AUDIT.md:135, AUDIT.md:52 (sentinel-match audit), FRESHNESS.md:69 (steward row), CHANGELOG.md:1237.

install_block.py teardown on a target file that does not exist exits 0 printing `absent: <target>; removed=0`, but first creates the target's parent folder and a `.<name>.afk.lock` file beside it; the SKILL.md teardown loop runs it for ${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/AGENTS.md even on a machine without that folder.

No register row or skill instruction invokes _atomic_write_locked or write_if_unchanged; within the partition documents they are named only by design records: GRILL-LOG.md:124 (extract install_block.py:105-224, which covers the lock helpers and _atomic_write_locked but not write_if_unchanged at :226-234), GRILL-LOG.md:141-143 and :142, and ADR design 0005 lines 1, 11, 15, 20 (the extracted 'safe writer'; the installer keeps raising its existing error so callers see exit 2). Enumerated: the seed name-form pass q-24def7a5 and the tracer case-blind untracked pass q-488bca1c over the partition documents, plus the prose pass q-e37c98c0.

developer_values.py is invoked by MANIFEST.md H6: the Probe runs `"$PY" "$DV" status` with no --repo from the repository root and parses stdout JSON `inherited` and `keys.<k>.need == "required"` with both stderrs dropped; the Fix runs `afk-python "$DV" status --repo <path>` (relies on keys main_checkout, configured, need, value, source, suggestion, missing, inherited, derived, and on exit 2 for a path that is not a git checkout) and `afk-python "$DV" set KEY=VALUE ... --repo <path>` with optional `--machine` (relies on exit 0 `developer_values: wrote <file>`, `KEY=` removing a key, `--machine` refusing a worktreeBasePath value with exit 2). SKILL.md step 2 runs the probe and step 3 runs Fix step 0 on every default and base run.

write_block is reached from documents only through `developer_values.py set` (record calls write_block at developer_values.py:208); it writes a fixed `<file>.tmp` then replaces, with no lock and no compare-before-write. Design records name it as the 'settings writer' that is to adopt the shared safe writer: GRILL-LOG.md:124, ADR design 0005 line 15.

setup_secrets.py is named by the `human:` Fix of MANIFEST.md H2 (line 76), S1 (746), C3 (422), C3b (441) and W5 (938), and by H2 Notes (87); SKILL.md step 4 (122-127) prints the command once for the human instead of running it. It takes no arguments and relies on: the caller's cwd inside the target checkout (else exit 1), CLAUDECODE unset (else exit 1), the P1 afk-python entry existing (else exit 1), and tracker/forge from the configuration; every abort is exit 1 via die, success exit 0.

SKILL.md:124 says setup_secrets.py 'refuses an agent shell: no tty'; the script's only refusal is CLAUDECODE being set (setup_secrets.py:147-148) and it has no tty test (the word appears only in its docstring at :11). The secret-step design locks the missing tty and PLUGIN_ROOT refusals (GRILL-LOG.md:110) and PRD AC-013 (PRD.md:92).

MANIFEST.md C3's human Fix names `glab auth login --hostname <host>`, but setup_secrets.py drives `glab auth login` (and `gh auth login`) with no host argument, leaving the host to the CLI's own prompt.

CHANGELOG.md:479-480 says setup_secrets.py 'warns instead of printing `tracker: none`'; the script still prints `tracker: <kind>   forge: <kind>` unconditionally and then warns when .afk/config.yaml is absent.

Design records about the secret step that the current code does not yet meet: GRILL-LOG.md:126 (re-read ~/.claude.json under a lock; today read at setup_secrets.py:185 and the start copy written at :252), ADR design 0004 line 14 (owner-only access, one backup; today a timestamped backup per run at :243-246 and no permission change).

install-git-hooks.sh is invoked by MANIFEST.md H5 Fix (`auto:` `bash "$AFK_PLUGIN_ROOT/hooks/install-git-hooks.sh"`, no arguments, run by SKILL.md step 4) and by SessionStart with `--quiet` (hooks/hooks.json:9, hooks/hooks.codex.json:9). H5 relies on the script's exit code only weakly: it exits 0 on success, on an already-current stub, outside a repository and when core.hooksPath is set, and 1 only for a pre-existing non-AFK hook without --quiet; the H5 Probe re-run decides 'fixed' by grepping the marker afk-branch-name-gate in <git-path hooks>/reference-transaction.

Consumers of the stub format install-git-hooks.sh writes, found by its markers rather than its name: the H5 probe (marker afk-branch-name-gate, MANIFEST.md:112), hooks/precommit-gates.sh:51-53 (marker afk-branch-name-gate plus the `gate="..."` line, install-git-hooks.sh:93), the H13 probe via background_git_hooks.py:26,81 (comment '(installed by afk-toolkit install-git-hooks.sh)', install-git-hooks.sh:90; documented at MANIFEST.md:343), and the tests scripts/tests/test_git_backstop.py:298-299 and scripts/tests/test_background_git_hooks.py:64.

Documents asserting install-git-hooks.sh behaviour, each checked against the script: PROVIDERS.md:116 and :119, hooks/README.md:8 and :106, AGENTS.md:200, MANIFEST.md:401, CHANGELOG.md:410, :2151, :2156, GRILL-LOG.md:10, :94, :140, providers/PARITY.md:116 (which gate covers it not read).

MANIFEST.md:968 (E table) lists hooks/install-git-hooks.sh as a consumer of AFK_PLUGIN_ROOT; the script reads it nowhere except a usage comment (install-git-hooks.sh:13) and resolves its root through afk_plugin_root in hooks/lib/provider.sh:64-75, and no file it loads reads AFK_PLUGIN_ROOT (in hooks/lib only adapter.sh:24, config.sh:22,39 and three Python modules do).
The H6 probe's inherited leg fails open: when `developer_values.py status` exits 2 its JSON is absent, the inline parser fails with stderr dropped, and the leg reports nothing inherited.
